summary: The single-board loopback host now resolves the bearer and checks the board grant on every read and rename. For a private board in an open workspace, a creator or subscriber may read; only a Member with that access may rename. Session, role and grant stay locked through the board operation. The host exposes no login endpoint or anonymous mode.
evidence: cargo test --locked --workspace --test loopback_board_access: both named cases passed, none ignored or filtered. Each used the production HTTP handler, generated in-memory credentials and a fresh schema in the explicit rustday_test database.

viewer_reads_but_cannot_rename: a subscribed Viewer read IDs 42 and 17 in order, both Review/1. A valid rename of 17 returned PermissionDenied (403). After revocation, the same client received SessionRejected (401) on both routes; requests without a bearer did too. Fresh store connections confirmed both original rows after each denial scenario.

member_edits_within_scope: the Member creator renamed only ID 17 from Review/1 to trimmed Coral/2. A fresh HTTP client and a fresh store connection agreed on both rows. A Member subscribed to another board could neither read nor edit this one. Making account_sessions unavailable returned AccessUnavailable (503) on both calls. After restoring the store and independently demoting the creator, the original client could still read but could not rename. Deleting the board policy denied access. Both committed rows and revisions stayed intact.

cargo test --locked --workspace: all 15 portable tests passed, including both prior HTTP reconnect/replay and rejection/correction cases using an authorized Member. Workspace and separately locked Android formatting checks passed, as did git diff --check.

Locked x86_64-linux-android cargo checks passed for the process probe and the separate Kit library. The feature-enabled host emulator harness also type-checked. The probe fixture supplies a signed-in Member via non-PTY stdin. The probe build reached linking but failed because the Android target linker was not configured (cc not found); no probe was run on a device.

No APK, emulator frame, connected Kit edit, HOME/resume, cold reopen or Windows window journey was exercised in this packet. The offline frame still uses only the packaged synthetic board. A connected Kit launch supplies no bearer and fails closed; its authenticated 07/08 journeys remain open. Windows direct-store development mode, other board kinds and roles, closed-workspace membership and native sign-in are outside this gate. The coordinator owns the reference comparison.
